factual_objections.claim: Referral rewards come out of gross profit, not the growth budget.
factual_objections.evidence: The stated $6,000 advertising allocation and $2,000 events allocation already exhaust the $8,000 monthly growth budget. Paying an additional month's billing per referred contract adds growth expenditure regardless of its funding source.
factual_objections.label: contradicted

factual_objections.claim: Successful ads can move to the full $8,000 while the paid referral program continues.
factual_objections.evidence: Allocating the entire stated growth budget to ads leaves nothing for the proposed $1,000 referral rewards and tools. Continuing those expenditures requires a revised allocation or additional funding.
factual_objections.label: contradicted

verdict.reason: Both offer a defensible ads-and-referrals test with a rep fallback. B initially budgets referral payouts, considers restrictions on property-manager incentives, and calculates replacement demand. A spends the entire budget before referral rewards and incorrectly treats those rewards as outside the growth budget. B also needs to reserve referral funding when scaling ads.
